options.name: Billionaire Romance
options.description: An eternal favorite. The male lead must be wealthy, powerful, and controlling, but with a wounded heart; the female lead is typically an ordinary person who is independent and strong.

options.name: Small Town Romance
options.description: The big-city protagonist returns to (or arrives in) a quiet small town for some reason, meeting a local 'warm-hearted' person (like a firefighter, sheriff, or veterinarian). Emphasizes community warmth and a slower pace of life.

options.name: Enemies to Lovers
options.description: Two people who initially despise each other are forced to interact due to work, accidents, etc., and sparks fly amidst their constant conflicts.

options.name: Fake Dating
options.description: Two people pretend to be a couple to deal with family, exes, or work, and end up falling in love for real.

options.name: Grumpy/Sunshine
options.description: One character is grumpy and taciturn, while the other is optimistic and cheerful like a little sun, eventually melting the other's heart.

options.name: Office Romance
options.description: A story between a boss and a subordinate, or two competitors.

options.name: Sports Romance
options.description: The protagonist is an athlete in sports like football, ice hockey, or baseball.

options.name: Mafia/Gang Romance
options.description: The male lead is a mafia boss, and the female lead is the daughter of a rival family or an innocent bystander.

options.name: Captive/Captor
options.description: The story revolves around a captor and their captive.

options.name: Bully Romance
options.description: The story takes place in high school or college, where the male lead initially bullies the female lead before falling for her.

options.name: Second Chance Romance
options.description: Childhood sweethearts or past lovers reconnect after years apart, exploring whether their old feelings can be rekindled.

options.name: Forced Proximity
options.description: Characters are trapped together in a confined space (elevator, cabin during a snowstorm, single hotel room) and must confront their feelings.

options.name: Secret Baby
options.description: One character has a child that the other character, the parent, doesn't know about. The revelation forces them to confront their past and future.

options.name: Amnesia
options.description: One character loses their memory, offering a 'clean slate' for a relationship to form or re-form, free from past baggage.

options.name: Marriage of Convenience
options.description: Two people marry for practical reasons (inheritance, visa, business deal) and unexpectedly fall in love.

options.name: Friends to Lovers
options.description: Two longtime friends slowly realize their feelings for each other are more than platonic.

options.name: Forbidden Love
options.description: A romance between people who shouldn't be together due to social status, family opposition, or other powerful external factors.

options.name: Love Triangle
options.description: The protagonist is torn between two compelling love interests.

options.name: Age Gap Romance
options.description: A significant age difference exists between the two main characters, creating unique challenges and dynamics.

options.name: Bodyguard Romance
options.description: One character is assigned to protect the other, leading to a romance complicated by duty and danger.

options.name: Celebrity/Normal Person
options.description: A famous movie star, musician, or public figure falls for an ordinary person, exploring the challenges of a public life.

options.name: Royalty Romance
options.description: A prince, princess, or other royal figure falls in love with a commoner.

options.name: Time Travel Romance
options.description: A character travels through time and finds love in a different era, facing the ultimate long-distance relationship challenge.

options.name: Paranormal Romance
options.description: The romance involves supernatural beings such as vampires, werewolves, angels, demons, or ghosts.

options.name: Medical Romance
options.description: Set in a hospital or clinic, focusing on the lives and loves of doctors and nurses.

options.name: Single Parent Romance
options.description: A single parent finds love again while navigating the complexities of family life.

options.name: Road Trip Romance
options.description: Two characters embark on a journey together, falling in love along the way.

options.name: Guardian/Ward
options.description: A classic trope where a guardian falls for their much younger ward, often fraught with taboo and power imbalance.

options.name: Dark Romance
options.description: Explores darker themes, often with morally ambiguous characters, dubious consent, and intense psychological elements.

options.name: Romantic Suspense
options.description: A romance plot combined with a thriller or mystery, where the characters must solve a crime or survive a threat while falling in love.

options.name: Historical Romance
options.description: A romance set in a specific historical period, from Regency England to the American West.

options.name: Sci-Fi Romance
options.description: Set in the future or on other planets, blending futuristic technology and speculative concepts with a love story.

options.name: Holiday Romance
options.description: The story is centered around a specific holiday, like Christmas, Valentine's Day, or Halloween, which acts as a catalyst for the romance.

options.name: Rockstar Romance
options.description: Focuses on the romantic relationship of a member of a famous band.

options.name: Secret Admirer
options.description: One character is secretly in love with the other and expresses their feelings anonymously through letters, gifts, or messages.

options.name: Mistaken Identity
options.description: One character is mistaken for someone else, leading to comedic or dramatic romantic complications.

options.name: Teacher/Student
options.description: A controversial trope involving a romantic relationship between an educator and their student (usually of legal age).

options.name: Revenge Plot
options.description: One character initially seeks revenge on the other, but ends up falling in love instead.

options.name: Arranged Marriage
options.description: Different from a marriage of convenience, this is often arranged by families for cultural or political reasons, and the couple must learn to love each other.

options.name: Soulmates/Fated Mates
options.description: The characters are destined to be together, a common theme in paranormal or fantasy romance.

options.name: Military Romance
options.description: One or both characters are in the military, dealing with deployment, duty, and the challenges of service life.

options.name: Cowboy Romance
options.description: Set in the American West, featuring cowboys, ranchers, and the rugged frontier lifestyle.

options.name: Motorcycle Club Romance
options.description: Romance within the gritty world of motorcycle clubs, often featuring alpha bikers and their women.

options.name: Prison Romance
options.description: A romance that develops when one character is incarcerated, exploring themes of redemption and second chances.

options.name: Firefighter Romance
options.description: Features brave firefighters risking their lives while finding love in their dangerous profession.

options.name: Police Officer Romance
options.description: Romance involving law enforcement officers, dealing with the dangers and stresses of police work.

options.name: Wilderness Survival Romance
options.description: Characters must survive in the wilderness together, forging a bond through shared hardship.

options.name: Casino/Gambling Romance
options.description: Set in the high-stakes world of casinos and gambling, with all its glamour and danger.

options.name: Auction/Contest Romance
options.description: One character is 'won' by the other through an auction or contest, leading to unexpected romance.

ending_tones: Happily Ever After (HEA): Clear victory, bright future, often with a wedding or proposal.
Happy For Now (HFN): They are together and happy, but the future isn't perfectly tied up.
Bittersweet: They may end up together, but with significant loss or sacrifice along the way.
Hopeful: They might not be officially together, but the path is clear for their future happiness.
Tragic: A rare ending in romance, where love does not conquer all and they are separated by circumstance or death.
Ironic: The character achieves their goal but at a cost that negates the victory.
Ambiguous/Open-ended: The story ends without a clear resolution, leaving the reader to interpret the outcome.
Cathartic: The ending provides a strong emotional release for the characters and reader, resolving deep-seated conflicts.
Inspiring: The protagonist overcomes all odds, leaving the reader feeling uplifted and motivated.
Ominous/Foreboding: The main conflict is resolved, but a new, darker threat looms on the horizon.
Triumphant: A resounding victory against all obstacles, celebrating love's power.
Peaceful: A quiet, serene conclusion where love brings inner tranquility.
Passionate: An intensely emotional ending filled with desire and deep connection.
Redemptive: Past mistakes are forgiven and characters find salvation through love.
Transformative: Characters are fundamentally changed for the better by their love.
Sacrificial: One character gives up something precious for the other's happiness.
Reunion: Long-separated lovers finally find their way back to each other.
New Beginning: The ending marks the start of a completely new chapter in life.
Healing: Love serves as the cure for deep emotional or physical wounds.
Liberating: Characters break free from constraints that held them back.
Magical: A fantastical element brings the lovers together in an otherworldly way.
Realistic: A grounded, believable ending that feels authentic to real life.
Shocking: An unexpected twist changes everything about the relationship.
Melancholic: A touching sadness mixed with joy about what was gained and lost.
Cyclical: The ending mirrors the beginning, showing how far the characters have come.
Community-centered: The entire community celebrates the couple's union.
Secret: The couple must keep their love hidden but are content in their private world.
Adventure-bound: The couple embarks on a new journey together.
Legacy: Their love creates something lasting that will impact future generations.
Spiritual: A transcendent connection that goes beyond the physical world.
Practical: A sensible, down-to-earth conclusion focused on building a life together.
Poetic: An artistically beautiful ending that reads like lyrical verse.
Humorous: A light-hearted, funny conclusion that leaves readers smiling.
Dramatic: A high-emotion finale with grand gestures and declarations.
Intimate: A private, personal moment between just the two lovers.
Celebratory: A joyous festival or party marks their commitment.
Protective: One character becomes the guardian of the other's dreams.
Domestic: The ending focuses on building a home and family together.
Career-focused: Their professional lives intertwine with their romantic success.
Travel-oriented: The couple explores the world together as their new adventure.
Philosophical: A thoughtful conclusion that explores the meaning of love.
Nostalgic: Looking back on their journey with appreciation and fondness.
Forward-looking: Focused entirely on the bright future ahead of them.
Unconventional: A unique ending that breaks traditional romance conventions.
Full-circle: Characters return to where they started but as changed people.
Cliffhanger: Leaves readers wanting more, suggesting ongoing adventures.
Epic: A grand, sweeping conclusion worthy of a legendary love story.
Minimalist: A simple, understated ending that speaks volumes through subtlety.
Explosive: High energy and intensity mark the final romantic culmination.
Gentle: A soft, tender conclusion that whispers rather than shouts.
